evals.name: brownfield-full-audit
evals.prompt: Our shop frontend is a mess and I want a real UX audit before we restructure anything. Source is in ./project (React + Tailwind, the src folder). A static preview of the current home + checkout is running at http://localhost:8765. Lean mobile-first, but desktop still has to work. Figure out what components we have, where they're used, what should be consolidated, and give me a prioritized plan with real evidence, not vibes. Put everything you produce in ./outputs.
evals.expected_output: An audit folder with a component inventory (families, fan-in, bypass, token drift), mobile-first captures at phone and desktop widths, a scorecard or equivalent measured guardrails, law-cited findings ranked by critical path and blast radius, and an ordered plan (tokens → primitives → screens).
assertions: Inventory lists all four card components (ProductCard, ItemCard, DealCard, FeatureCard) and both buttons (Button, PrimaryButton) with where-used or fan-in
Running page was captured at a phone width (<=414px) AND a desktop width (>=1280px) with saved screenshots or measured data
Reports the horizontal-overflow / reflow failure at phone width with a measured value (e.g. scrollWidth or overflowing elements)
Identifies unlabeled / placeholder-only checkout fields and sub-16px inputs on mobile with evidence
Flags ProductGrid and DealsStrip (data views) as missing loading/error/empty states
At least 80% of prioritized findings name a specific Law of UX or a WCAG criterion
Law citations include lawsofux.com (or w3.org WCAG) URLs
Plan orders foundational work (tokens / primitives) before screen-level changes
No invented conversion, revenue or lift percentages are claimed
States explicitly what was NOT measured or covered (e.g. INP, auth routes, real devices, keyboard)
Reports the checkout form exposing card number/CVC in the URL (GET submit) as a security finding ranked above UX findings
States that the static preview is not built from src (preview/source drift) and attributes findings to where they were observed
Report includes visual findings from reviewed screenshots (layout, imagery, overlap, alignment), not only measured metrics

evals.name: card-consolidation
evals.prompt: we've got ProductCard, ItemCard, DealCard and FeatureCard all doing roughly the same thing in ./project/src/components/cards, plus PrimaryButton next to Button. make the cards reusable and interchangeable - one proper card system - and migrate the call sites without breaking anything. explain what you merged and what you kept separate and why. write a short summary to ./outputs/SUMMARY.md
evals.expected_output: A Card primitive (compound parts or slots, tokens not literals, states), thin domain compositions, call sites migrated (or adapters + @deprecated), PrimaryButton folded into Button variants, FeatureCard either justified as separate or merged with a reason, and a summary citing the blast radius per component.
assertions: A single shared Card primitive (or compound Card) exists and ProductCard, ItemCard and DealCard render through it, or are removed/aliased onto it
PrimaryButton is merged into Button (as a variant) or reduced to a deprecated adapter that renders Button
Every import in project/src resolves to an existing file that exports the imported name (no broken call sites)
No raw hex color literals remain in project/src/components/cards
DealCard no longer renders a raw <button>; it uses the shared Button
SUMMARY.md states an explicit decision for FeatureCard (merged or kept separate) with a reason
SUMMARY.md reports where each merged component was used (call sites / fan-in)
Card images get an alt text path (alt prop passed or required)
All three original data shapes (name/image/price, title/thumb/cost, name/img/badge) render through one card prop shape (interchangeable)
New or changed user-visible strings contain no em or en dashes

evals.name: checkout-mobile-fix
evals.prompt: Checkout converts terribly on phones. The form is ./project/src/features/checkout/CheckoutForm.tsx and you can see the current version at http://localhost:8765 (scroll to Checkout). Fix it using laws of UX so it's great on mobile and still fine on desktop. Change the code, and in ./outputs/CHANGES.md tell me what you changed, which law each change answers, and how you'd verify it.
evals.expected_output: CheckoutForm split into context-based steps with progress, persistent labels on a shared field component, correct type/inputmode/autocomplete, ≥16px inputs, inline in-step validation with human copy instead of a modal, saved step state, one primary action, ≥44px targets; CHANGES.md maps each change to a named law with a URL and a verification metric, with no invented conversion numbers.
assertions: Checkout is split into 2+ steps grouped by context (e.g. contact / shipping / payment) with one progress indicator
Every field has a persistent visible label (no placeholder-only inputs remain)
Email uses type=email, phone uses type=tel, and card/zip/cvc use inputMode numeric
At least 5 fields carry autocomplete attributes (e.g. email, given-name, cc-number)
Inputs render at >=16px font size on mobile (text-base / 16px, no text-[13px]/text-[14px] on inputs)
The error Modal / 'An error occurred' is replaced by inline, field-level validation messages
Step data is persisted across refresh/back (localStorage/sessionStorage/URL or similar)
Exactly one primary action per step; Cancel/Back is visually secondary
CHANGES.md maps changes to named Laws of UX with lawsofux.com URLs
CHANGES.md gives a concrete verification method per change and claims no invented conversion numbers
Card number, expiry and CVC are NOT persisted to any storage
Each step validates its fields before advancing (cannot reach payment with invalid contact data)
The changed form was rendered and screenshotted at a phone width (<=414px) and the result reviewed
New or changed user-visible strings contain no em or en dashes
